The system shall support an admin-set interval for periodic update checks.
The system shall always allow a manual update check when the user has permission.
The system shall suppress update checks entirely when the machine is offline by policy.
The system shall suppress update checks entirely during a maintenance freeze.
The system shall suppress update checks entirely when the organization has explicitly disabled outbound update traffic.
If the system is marked as locked down, update check behavior shall follow the admin policy.
Changing permissions shall require confirmation when it affects shared files or system locations.
The confirmation prompt shall help the user understand the consequence instead of presenting a generic yes-or-no prompt.
When full history is not available, the system shall hide or redact sensitive names, paths, and protected content by default instead of exposing them.
For comparison or metadata views, the system shall provide a reduced detail set that includes counts, sizes, timestamps, and status markers so users can work without seeing restricted information.
If the user has the required permissions, the system may allow a fuller view or export.
Any fuller view or export shall follow the same access rules as the source data.
The system shall not reveal sensitive fields merely because a comparison or export is requested.
The product shall stop the operation immediately when the external tool returns an error, partial output, or output that cannot be confidently parsed.
If partial output has already been created and it cannot be clearly identified as safe and usable, the product shall quarantine it or leave it untouched for the user to review.
The product shall avoid committing already-started archive changes as final unless the tool returned a result that can be trusted.
The product shall leave the original data intact whenever possible after an external tool error, partial output, or unparseable output.
After showing the error, the product shall require the user to decide what to do next.
Before allowing any retry, overwrite, or deletion, the system shall offer the user options to view the log or error details, keep the current files unchanged, or abandon the operation.
If the archive format supports splitting and the user has enabled splitting, splitting shall be the first fallback.
Streaming shall be used when the tool and archive type support it and the input comes from a source that does not need to be fully staged first.
If none of the fallback options are safe or supported, the product shall stop early with a clear message instead of trying to continue and risking a failed or partial archive.
The system shall state that no data was intentionally changed yet.
The system shall instruct the user to reduce the scope.
The system shall instruct the user to choose a format that supports splitting or streaming.
The system shall instruct the user to adjust the settings if the user's policy allows it.
If any temporary files were created, the system shall state whether they were kept for review or cleaned up.
The system shall indicate whether there is anything to recover.
For the highest-risk actions, the system should provide an additional "I understand" style checkbox.
